stem.text: A vertical shaft is drilled to an unknown depth D meters, where \( D > 3 \). The amount of dissolved salt per meter of depth is \( f(h) = \sin{\left(\frac{h^{2}}{5} \right)} + 5 \) grams per meter for \( 0 \le h \le 3 \), where h is the depth in meters. Below depth 3 the amount per meter is an unknown continuous function g(h), and \( 0 \le g(h) \le 6 e^{3 - h} \) for \( h \ge 3 \), and \( \int_{3}^{\infty} 6 e^{3 - h}\,dh = 6 \). Let T be the total amount of dissolved salt, in grams, along the whole shaft. Write an expression involving integrals for T, and explain why \( T \le 23 \). Use a calculator for any numerical work.

answer_key.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{3} f(h)\,dh + \int_{3}^{D} g(h)\,dh \), and \( T \le 23 \) because \( \int_{0}^{3} f(h)\,dh \approx 16.424 \) and \( \int_{3}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{3}^{\infty} 6 e^{3 - h}\,dh = 6 \).

worked_solution.text: The model changes at depth 3, so split the total there: \( T = \int_{0}^{3} f(h)\,dh + \int_{3}^{D} g(h)\,dh \).
Since \( 0 \le g(h) \le 6 e^{3 - h} \) and the interval from 3 to D lies inside the interval from 3 to infinity, \( \int_{3}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le 6 \). So \( T \le 16.424 + 6 < 23 \).
